drills.title: Tee Height Reset
drills.problem: Driver launching too high — losing distance and carry efficiency
drills.drill: Drop your tee height by half an inch. Place an alignment stick flat on the ground under the ball path. Focus on catching the ball on the upswing by moving the ball 1 inch forward of your normal position. Hit 10 shots feeling like you're launching off a ramp, not chopping down.
drills.cue: Sweep up through it — feel the club head rise before impact

drills.title: In-to-Out Path Drill (Driver)
drills.problem: High launch + left start = steep over-the-top path, likely pulling with added loft
drills.drill: Put an alignment stick in the ground at 45° just outside your right foot, angled away from you. Practice swinging under and past the stick without touching it — this forces an in-to-out path. Combine with a low tee. 3 slow-motion swings, then 7 real shots.
drills.cue: Start the ball right of the target, let it draw back

drills.title: Stack and Tilt Entry Drill
drills.problem: High launch + right start = too much secondary axis tilt at address, flipping through impact
drills.drill: Set up with your sternum slightly forward of normal (over the ball vs behind it). Feel like your weight stays 60% on your lead side even at the top. This reduces dynamic loft and helps square the face. Hit 10 shots with that forward sternum feel.
drills.cue: Chest stays over the ball — don't fall back

drills.title: Upswing Launch Drill
drills.problem: Driver launching too low — ball coming off too hot with low trajectory, wind exposure
drills.drill: Tee the ball higher than normal so the equator of the ball sits above the crown of the driver. Move ball position to just inside your front heel. Practice making 5 rehearsal swings where you feel the club bottom out 4 inches behind the ball and sweep up. Hit 10 shots.
drills.cue: Hit up on it — feel the club head climbing at impact

drills.title: Axis Tilt Recovery Drill
drills.problem: Low launch + left = driver path too far left with delofted face, steep and pulling
drills.drill: Place a headcover 6 inches behind the ball on the target line. Practice swinging without hitting the headcover — this forces a shallower approach. Focus on your right shoulder staying back and under, not driving toward the ball. Tee up high. Hit 10 shots.
drills.cue: Right shoulder stays low and back — shallow the entry

drills.title: Face Rotation Drill (Driver)
drills.problem: Low launch + right = open face at impact, ball starting right with low spin and low angle
drills.drill: Hold the club with your lead hand only and make 10 slow swings focusing on rotating the face closed through impact. Then hit 5 shots with both hands, feeling the same forearm rotation. Tee high. The goal is to get the face squaring up earlier.
drills.cue: Feel the logo on your glove rotate toward the sky post-impact

drills.title: Low Spin Contact Drill
drills.problem: Driver spin too high — ballooning, losing distance, especially in wind
drills.drill: Put a small piece of impact tape on the face. Hit 10 shots and check where you're striking it. High spin almost always means strikes on the top of the face or toe. Focus on finding the center-low contact. Feel like you're hitting 'through' the ball with the center of the face, not glancing.
drills.cue: Center-low contact kills spin — find the sweet spot

drills.title: Spin Rate Restoration Drill
drills.problem: Driver spin too low — ball falling out of sky early, no carry
drills.drill: Loft up 1–2 degrees on the hosel if adjustable. If not, work on catching the ball slightly higher on the face (top 1/3) by teeing 1/4 inch higher. Hit 10 shots with a slightly steeper angle of attack feeling. Low spin with low VLA = no lift at all.
drills.cue: Catch it higher on the face — more dynamic loft

drills.title: Ball Back Fairway Drill
drills.problem: Fairway wood launching too high — losing distance, steep angle of attack
drills.drill: Move the ball back 1 inch in your stance. Feel like you're 'trapping' it at the bottom of your arc, not scooping. Place a tee in the ground where the ball was and practice clipping the new tee position with ball moved back. 10 shots.
drills.cue: Trap it at the bottom — no scoop

drills.title: Outside-In Path Fix (Fairway)
drills.problem: Fairway wood going high and left — over-the-top path with added loft
drills.drill: Set two alignment sticks in a gate — one just inside the target line at address width, one just outside. Practice swinging through the gate without hitting the inner stick on the downswing. This forces an in-to-out path. 3 slow swings, then 7 real shots.
drills.cue: Swing out to the right side of the fairway at impact

drills.title: Release Timing Drill (Fairway)
drills.problem: Fairway wood going high and right — holding off the release, open face
drills.drill: Hit 10 shots trying to start the ball 10 yards left of target. This forces early forearm rotation and a closed face. Don't aim left — just swing with intention to release early. Compare the actual HLA. You should see the ball start moving toward center.
drills.cue: Release early — turn the face over through impact

drills.title: Sweep and Launch Drill
drills.problem: Fairway wood launching too low — hitting down too much, killing carry
drills.drill: Place a tee in the ground 4 inches in front of the ball on the target line. Your goal is to clip that forward tee after you hit the ball — this proves a shallowing, sweeping path. Ball forward in stance. 10 shots.
drills.cue: Sweep through it — feel like you're brushing grass forward

drills.title: Path and Loft Recovery (Fairway)
drills.problem: Low launch + left start from fairway = delofted and over the top — worst combo
drills.drill: Drop down to a 7-iron and hit 5 high draws to reset your delivery feel. Then come back to the fairway wood. The 7-iron exaggerates the correct release and shallowing. When you return to the wood, try to replicate that same 'around and through' feeling.
drills.cue: Shallow the downswing — come from inside and release

drills.title: Face Square Drill (Fairway)
drills.problem: Low launch + right = steep and open face — a pushed low shot
drills.drill: Set up with an alignment stick pointing at your target. Hit 5 shots trying to start every ball online or left of the stick. If the ball starts right — open face at impact. Practice closing the face in your grip setup (rotate both hands slightly clockwise) then hit 10 shots.
drills.cue: Strengthen grip slightly — feel the face close at impact

drills.title: Handle Forward Impact Drill
drills.problem: Long iron launching too high — flipping at impact, adding loft at the wrong time
drills.drill: Place a golf glove under your lead armpit and keep it there through impact. This stops the chicken wing and keeps the handle leading. Hit 10 shots with the glove drill. The ball should launch noticeably lower and more penetrating.
drills.cue: Handle leads the face — feel the shaft lean forward at impact

drills.title: Path Fix + Handle Lead (Long Iron)
drills.problem: Long iron high and left — over-the-top with flip, double trouble
drills.drill: Choke down 2 inches on the grip. Place a headcover just outside the ball on the target line — hit the ball without touching the headcover. Choking down shortens the arc and forces a more downward, in-to-out strike. 10 shots.
drills.cue: Short and steep is wrong — long and shallow from inside

drills.title: Swing Left Release Drill
drills.problem: Long iron high and right — path going too far right, holding off the face
drills.drill: Pick a target 20 yards left of your actual target. Swing toward that left target aggressively. Don't fear the ball going left — the open face will keep it on line. After 5 shots like this, go back to your real target. Feel how much more rotation you have.
drills.cue: Swing hard left — rotation fixes the height and direction

drills.title: Low Point Forward Drill
drills.problem: Long iron launching too low — hitting too far past center, delofting excessively
drills.drill: Place a tee 1 inch in front of the ball. Practice striking the ball first AND then the tee. If you're launching low with center HLA, you're hitting down TOO aggressively. Work on shallowing out — ball slightly more forward. 10 shots with the forward tee target.
drills.cue: Down + forward, not just down — keep the loft working

drills.title: Gate Drill — Shallow and Square
drills.problem: Long iron low and left — steep path, closed face, toe strike likely
drills.drill: Build a 2-tee gate just wider than your clubhead. Practice swinging through the gate without disturbing either tee. Gate forces a shallower entry. After 5 gate swings (no ball), hit 5 real shots. Focus on path — the low-left combo is usually steep + too much rotation.
drills.cue: Let the path shallow — turn the body, don't force the arms

drills.title: Grip Pressure Release Drill
drills.problem: Long iron low and right — block, open face, tight grip holding off release
drills.drill: Hit 5 shots with grip pressure at 3/10 — barely holding the club. The low grip tension forces the face to naturally square through forearm rotation. You'll feel the face closing and the ball starting left. Gradually increase tension and maintain that release feel on 10 real shots.
drills.cue: Soft grip = natural release = square face

drills.title: Strike Down Drill (Mid Iron)
drills.problem: Mid iron launching too high — scooping, thin strikes, or ball too far forward
drills.drill: Tee a ball very low to the ground (half-tee). Your only job is to clip it cleanly. If you scoop, you'll pop the tee without clipping the ball cleanly. Hit 10 low-tee shots focusing on a descending strike that takes the tee out. Then hit 5 off the ground.
drills.cue: Clip the tee — hands ahead, strike down

drills.title: Feet Together Drill (Mid Iron)
drills.problem: Mid iron high and left — over-the-top, steep, too much body drive left
drills.drill: Hit 10 shots with your feet together (touching). This eliminates lateral slide and forces rotation as your only power source. High-left patterns almost always involve a lateral body thrust — feet together stops it cold. After 10, widen stance and carry the rotation feel.
drills.cue: Rotate around your spine — not slide toward target

drills.title: Pump Drill — Slot and Release
drills.problem: Mid iron high and right — coming over-the-top but with open face, a weak fade/push
drills.drill: At the top of your backswing, 'pump' the club down 6 inches toward your right pocket (slot it) before transitioning into the forward swing. Do this 3 times in slow motion, then hit a ball. This shallows the club and keeps the face from opening. 10 shots.
drills.cue: Drop it into the slot before you hit — right pocket first

drills.title: Towel Behind Ball Drill
drills.problem: Mid iron launching too low — excessive forward shaft lean, killing dynamic loft
drills.drill: Place a folded towel 4 inches behind the ball. Make a full swing and hit the ball WITHOUT touching the towel. If you hit the towel, you're coming in too steeply. This drill teaches a shallower delivery that preserves loft. 10 shots.
drills.cue: Miss the towel — shallower entry, more loft at impact

drills.title: Right Hand Release Drill
drills.problem: Mid iron low and left — steep path, closed face, too aggressive a roll through
drills.drill: Hit 10 shots with right hand only on the club. Single-hand forces proper wrist mechanics — you can't muscle it steep. After 5 right-hand-only shots, reconnect both hands and replicate the feel. The ball should launch higher and the left miss should clear up.
drills.cue: Right hand only — find the correct wrist release naturally

drills.title: Clockface Path Drill
drills.problem: Mid iron low and right — block with open face and steep delivery
drills.drill: Imagine a clockface on the ground. Your swing path should exit toward 7 o'clock (slightly left of target). Currently it's exiting toward 4–5 o'clock (right of target). Place a stick at 7 o'clock position and practice swinging toward it. The left-exit path naturally squares the face and adds loft. 10 shots.
drills.cue: Swing to 7 o'clock — left exit, not right

drills.title: Knockdown Wedge Drill
drills.problem: Wedge launching too high — scooping, flipping, no compression on short shots
drills.drill: Choke down 2 inches. Move ball back in stance by 1 ball width. Hit 10 'knockdown' wedges where the ball flight stays below 20 feet. This forces a trapped, compressed strike. Then hit 5 normal wedges and feel the same compression but with full loft. Check your VLA — it should drop significantly.
drills.cue: Compress and trap — hands forward, low flight

drills.title: Open Face Recovery Drill (Wedge)
drills.problem: Wedge high and left — flippy release with path going left, pulling shots that balloon
drills.drill: Open your stance 15 degrees but keep the face square to your original target. Hit 10 shots. This exaggerates the left path but forces the face to stay open relative to path — you'll feel the difference between path and face. After 10, close the stance back and notice the natural release. 10 more shots.
drills.cue: Face controls the height — path controls direction

drills.title: Lead Hand Rotation Drill (Wedge)
drills.problem: Wedge high and right — flipping with open face, a push-balloon
drills.drill: Hit 10 wedges with lead hand only. Focus on the back of your lead hand facing the target at impact (not sky-facing). This is the correct wrist position for a square face. High-right wedge shots almost always mean the back of the lead hand is facing up at impact. Fix it with one hand.
drills.cue: Back of lead hand faces target — not the sky

drills.title: Loft Preservation Drill
drills.problem: Wedge launching too low — too much shaft lean, killing bounce and loft
drills.drill: Address the ball with the shaft vertical (no forward lean) and make 5 half-swings. Feel how the face opens and loft increases. Now return to your normal setup but reduce shaft lean by 2 inches. Hit 10 wedges. Wedges need 4–6 degrees of lean max — not 15+.
drills.cue: Less shaft lean — let the loft of the club do the work

drills.title: Steep Path Reset Drill (Wedge)
drills.problem: Wedge low and left — too steep, too closed, killing bounce — worst for full wedges
drills.drill: Take a pitching wedge and hit 10 chips from 20 yards. No full swing. Focus purely on a soft, square impact where the face is looking at the flag at impact. Then take a full wedge swing at 60% speed keeping that same 'face up' feel. Hit 10 full shots.
drills.cue: Soft hands, face to flag — don't roll through it

drills.title: Hip Rotation Clear Drill
drills.problem: Wedge low and right — hips stalling, arms getting trapped, push with low launch
drills.drill: At address, feel your lead hip already slightly open (pre-rotated). Hit 10 wedges where your first move is to fire the lead hip open — before your arms move. The hips leading will un-trap the arms and get the face squaring. Low-right wedges are almost always a hip-stall pattern.
drills.cue: Lead hip fires first — clear the body, free the arms

drills.title: Contact Quality Drill (Spin Control)
drills.problem: Wedge spinning too high — could be a clean grooves + descending path issue, or thin strikes
drills.drill: Check your grooves first — clean them with a groove brush. Then hit 10 shots focusing on hitting the bottom half of the ball (not center). A slightly lower contact point on the face reduces spin on full wedges. Compare spin across the session. If ball is striking high on the face, move ball back 1/2 inch.
drills.cue: Clean grooves, bottom-half contact — control the spin

drills.title: Compression and Groove Drill
drills.problem: Wedge not spinning enough — ball releasing too far, hard to hold greens
drills.drill: Wedge spin comes from: (1) clean grooves, (2) clean ball, (3) compressed contact. Clean your grooves now. Use a new ball. Hit 10 shots focusing on a crisp, slightly descending blow — you should hear a sharp 'click', not a 'thud'. Low spin is almost always contact quality or dirty equipment.
drills.cue: Sharp click = compressed spin contact — hear the difference

drills.title: Anti-Pull Path Drill
drills.problem: Consistent pull or pull-hook — severe over-the-top, path way left of target
drills.drill: Place an alignment stick in the ground pointing at 3 o'clock (directly right). Hit 10 shots where your finish position has the club pointing at or right of that stick. This is extreme exaggeration — your current path is so left that you need to feel 'wildly right' to get to center. Build up over 3 sessions.
drills.cue: Finish to the right — feel ridiculous doing it

drills.title: Anti-Slice Path Drill
drills.problem: Consistent push or push-slice — path too far right, open face through impact
drills.drill: Place an alignment stick 2 feet outside the ball on the target line (outside). Hit 10 shots without touching the stick on the follow-through. This forces your swing path to exit left of the stick — in-to-out to slightly out-to-in. The natural result is a squarer face and centered start line.
drills.cue: Exit left of the stick — path correction first, face follows

drills.title: Metronome Tempo Drill
drills.problem: Shots scattering everywhere — no consistent pattern, tempo and sequencing issue
drills.drill: Use a metronome app at 72 BPM. Every beat is one count. Backswing = 2 beats (count 1-2), downswing = 1 beat (count 3). Hit 15 shots at exactly this tempo. Scattershot patterns almost always come from inconsistent tempo — some shots rushed, some held. The metronome forces a 2:1 back-to-through ratio.
drills.cue: 2 beats back, 1 beat through — every single swing

drills.title: Pre-Shot Routine Lock Drill
drills.problem: Inconsistent scatter pattern — no pre-shot routine, setup varying between shots
drills.drill: Build a 30-second pre-shot routine: (1) Stand behind ball, pick intermediate target 3 feet ahead. (2) Walk in from the side, align clubface to intermediate target. (3) Set feet. (4) One forward press trigger. (5) Go. Hit 20 shots with this exact routine — same time every time. Scatter closes dramatically with consistent setup.
drills.cue: Same routine = same result — no routine = no repeatability

drills.title: Tighten the Window Drill
drills.problem: Good pattern — now make the window tighter
drills.drill: You're in the zone for this club. Now make it smaller. Set a target flag or cone. Hit 20 shots aiming to land within 5 yards left/right of the flag. Track how many you hit. Your goal: 15/20 inside the window. If you're already there — tighten to 3 yards. This is competitive pressure simulation.
drills.cue: Good isn't good enough — make the window smaller

drills.title: Competitive Pressure Simulation
drills.problem: Pattern is solid — need to maintain it under pressure
drills.drill: Hit 10 shots with normal routine. Now hit 10 more where each shot has a consequence: if it misses the window, you do 5 pushups before the next shot. The mild stress activates the same physiological response as competition. Your scores with and without pressure should be within 2–3 shots of each other at your skill level.
drills.cue: Stay in your routine under stress — process over result

drills.title: Speed and Compression Drill
drills.problem: Carrying short of baseline — losing distance somewhere in the chain
drills.drill: Step 1: Hit 5 shots at 70% effort, focus only on center contact. Step 2: Hit 5 at 85% effort, same contact focus. Step 3: Hit 5 at 100% effort. Compare your carry on each set. If the 70% shots carry close to the 100% shots — you're losing energy through impact, not generating it. The fix is a rotation and hip speed drill, not grip pressure.
drills.cue: Speed comes from rotation — not arms and grip

drills.title: Attack Angle Calibration Drill
drills.problem: Iron spinning too high — likely steep attack angle, not necessarily bad contact
drills.drill: Move the ball 1 inch forward in your stance. This naturally shallows the attack angle because your low point shifts back relative to the ball. A shallower angle of attack with the same speed = significantly less spin. Hit 10 shots with the ball forward and compare. You should see spin drop without losing distance.
drills.cue: Ball forward = shallower AoA = less spin

drills.title: Descending Blow Recovery Drill
drills.problem: Iron spinning too low — thin contact, sweeping, not compressing the ball
drills.drill: Place a coin 1 inch in front of the ball. Your goal is to take a divot that starts at the coin and goes forward (past it). If your divot is behind the coin — you're hitting up on it. The coin drill confirms you're catching ball-first. Low spin irons are almost always thin/sweeping contacts. 15 shots with coin.
drills.cue: Divot starts after the coin — ball first, dirt second
